title: _verify_static_source_schema treats a bare `schema` key as a schema declaration the read adapter never honors, causing a no-op file read
description: `has_schema_declaration` (lines 173-175) gates the verification read on the presence of any of `schema_overrides`, `dtypes`, `column_dtypes`, or `schema`. For the first three, the read is meaningful: `read_data_source` -> `build_data_source_adapter` -> `_schema_overrides_from_config` (src/haute/_io.py:127-138) recognizes exactly `schema_overrides`/`dtypes`/`column_dtypes` and runs `_validate_declared_schema` during the read, so declared-dtype drift is enforced at the deploy boundary. But `_schema_overrides_from_config` does NOT recognize a bare `schema` key. So a static dataSource whose config carries only `schema` (and no `expected_columns`, no schema_overrides/dtypes/column_dtypes) passes the gate, performs a full `read_data_source(...).collect_schema()` whose `actual` is then discarded (the `if expected and ...` block at line 199 is skipped because `expected` is falsy), and validates nothing. The result is wasted deploy-time I/O plus a false impression that the `schema` declaration is being enforced, when it is silently ignored. This is an inconsistency between the gate's recognized keys and the adapter's recognized keys.
evidence:
Gate at lines 173-176:
    has_schema_declaration = any(
        key in config for key in ("schema_overrides", "dtypes", "column_dtypes", "schema")
    )
    if not expected and not has_schema_declaration:
        return
Adapter recognition at src/haute/_io.py:127-138 (`_schema_overrides_from_config`) keys on only `schema_overrides`/`dtypes`/`column_dtypes` — `schema` is absent. With config={'schema': {...}} and no expected_columns: line 176 does not early-return, lines 183-189 read+compute `actual`, line 199 `if expected and ...` is False, function returns having enforced nothing.
